column1: The literature in monetary economics has analyzed several alternative assumptions about the relationship between monetary and fiscal policies. In most traditional analyses, fiscal policy is assumed to adjust to ensure that the government’s intertemporal budget is always in balance while monetary policy is free to set the nominal money stock or the nominal rate of interest. This situation is described as one of monetary dominance, or one in which fiscal policy is passive and monetary policy is active (Leeper 1991). The models of chapters 2 and 3 implicitly fall into this category in that fiscal policy was ignored and monetary policy determined the price level.
